turns.query: I need in vitro to in vivo extrapolation (IVIVE) for hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs. I want predicted CLh (hepatic clearance mL/min/kg) and extraction ratio for each compound.
turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — Scales in vitro microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance for 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs using well-stirred and parallel-tube models.

Input: Compound CSV with CLint (µL/min/mg microsomal protein), molecular weight, and fu,inc for your 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs (e.g., imatinib, dasatinib, bosutinib, ponatinib)
Key steps:

CLint scaling → PKNCA/IVIVE engine applies microsomal scaling factors (MPPGL × liver weight) to compute scaled CLint
Well-stirred + parallel-tube models → predicted CLh (mL/min/kg) and hepatic extraction ratio (Eh) per compound


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg + Eh per compound) + clearance_summary.json (model comparison, well-stirred vs. parallel-tube)

Decision gate: Flag compounds with Eh > 0.7 as high-extraction (CLh highly sensitive to hepatic blood flow, not fu,p) and Eh < 0.3 as low-extraction (CLh sensitive to fu,p and intrinsic clearance) — critical for predicting dose linearity and DDI risk in the BCR-ABL1 TKI series.

turns.responseText:
IVIVE Hepatic Clearance — BCR-ABL1 TKI Panel — Scales measured microsomal CLint to predicted human hepatic clearance (CLh) and extraction ratio (Eh) for 4 TKIs using the well-stirred liver model.

Input: 4 BCR-ABL1 TKIs with measured CLint (Dasatinib 220, Bosutinib 60, Imatinib 25, Nilotinib 12 µL/min/mg), fu_plasma (0.04, 0.03, 0.04, 0.01), fu_mic = 1.0, Qh = 20.7 mL/min/kg
Key steps:

IVIVE scaling engine → applies MPPGL (45 mg/g) × liver weight (25.7 g/kg) to convert CLint_microsomal to scaled CLint_in vivo (mL/min/kg) per compound
Well-stirred model → computes CLh = Qh × (fu_plasma × CLint) / (Qh + fu_plasma × CLint) and Eh = CLh / Qh for each TKI


Expected output: ivive_results.csv (CLh mL/min/kg + Eh per compound across all 4 TKIs) + clearance_summary.json (model parameters, scaling factors, extraction class per compound)

Decision gate: Flag Dasatinib as high-extraction (Eh > 0.7 anticipated given CLint = 220 µL/min/mg) — CLh will approach Qh and be flow-limited, making dose predictions insensitive to fu_plasma changes; flag Nilotinib as low-extraction candidate (Eh < 0.3 anticipated) — CLh will be binding- and enzyme-sensitive, elevating DDI risk with CYP3A4 inhibitors.

ABL1 Kinase Pharmacophore Model & Library Screen — Builds a consensus pharmacophore from 4 known ABL1 inhibitors and screens a 4-compound library for feature-matched hits in a single workflow.


Input: Reference SMILES (Imatinib, Dasatinib, Bosutinib, Asciminib) + Library SMILES (Gleevec-analog-1, Ponatinib, Terfenadine, Acetaminophen); min_features = 3


Key steps:

RDKit/MolVS feature extraction → consensus pharmacophore model (HBD, HBA, aromatic ring, hydrophobic center features derived from all 4 actives)
Pharmacophore screen → each library compound scored against model, filtered at min_features ≥ 3 threshold → feature-match score per compound



Expected output: filtered_hits.csv (compounds passing the pharmacophore filter with per-feature match scores) + pharmacophore_model.json (feature definitions + coordinates) + HTML visual report ranking all 4 library compounds


Decision gate: Compounds must match ≥ 3 pharmacophore features to advance — expect Gleevec-analog-1 and Ponatinib to pass (ABL1-like scaffold), while Acetaminophen (single amide, MW 151) is predicted to fail; Terfenadine borderline pending aromatic/HBA overlap.

Input: 30-row assay CSV (15 compounds × 2 assay types: IC50_BCR_ABL1 in nM + hERG_IC50 in µM, dated 2026-03-15)

CSV parser + unit normalizer → pivoted compound matrix (all values converted to µM)
Composite scorer (log-scaled BCR-ABL1 potency + hERG selectivity index = hERG IC50 / BCR-ABL1 IC50) → ranked compound table
HTML report generator → ranked leaderboard with traffic-light safety flags (🟢 / 🟡 / 🔴)


Expected output: ranked_compounds.csv (rank, composite score, BCR-ABL1 IC50, hERG IC50, selectivity index) + campaign_summary.json + interactive HTML report with per-compound safety badges

Decision gate: hERG IC50 < 1 µM → 🔴 cardiac risk flag (auto-deprioritized); BCR-ABL1 IC50 < 10 nM → potency pass threshold. CPD009 (hERG 0.08 µM) and CPD010 (hERG 0.05 µM) are expected to rank last; CPD004–CPD006 (sub-nM BCR-ABL1, hERG ≥ 30 µM) are expected to rank #1–2.
